notes: VXX is an index/breadth symbol per semantics.md §3, so its bid/ask MUST be
null even though the wire carries 449.99/450.01 like every other frame.
This is the rule a new binding is most likely to miss, and the reason this
seq is per-symbol and shared between kinds (semantics.md §6.1): SPY runs
1, 2, 3 with the bar_1m taking 3. All six frames carry one sid.
The harness reuses the tick timestamp (13:30:45) for EL_PublishTickEx, so
this fixture exercises semantics.md §2.1: bucket_start is floored to the
minute, giving 17:30:00Z rather than 17:30:45Z. Real EL supplies an already
aligned time, which makes the flooring a no-op and easy to leave unwritten —
it was, until this fixture caught it.
The wire carries bid/ask on bar_1m too, and they are recorded here, but the
reference Python binding's Bar type does not model them — that data is
dropped. A binding that does keep them has something to check against; one
that drops them is not wrong, only lossier. Worth deciding deliberately
Only wire-derivable fields are asserted. Anything a binding computes on top
(VWAP, session tagging, aggregation) is outside the contract.
